structured_output.what_is_happening: 济公 (Ji Gong, the Chinese folk-hero monk) is a 35-minute-old token. Its pool was created directly on PumpSwap: migrated_unix is 0 and no launchpad is listed, so the creator appears to have supplied liquidity that is not locked (0% LP burned). The price is up about 530-630% in one hour on about $1M of volume, against about $57k of liquidity. The trading pattern looks manufactured. In the last 5 minutes buys and sells were exactly equal (141/141 on DexScreener, 136/136 on a later fetch), with 48 unique buyers and 49 unique sellers. That suggests a small set of wallets recycling volume. GeckoTerminal counts 1,917 unique buyers but only 50 unique sellers. About 1,300 of those buyers appeared 15-30 minutes ago and only 49 in the last 15 minutes, which looks like a burst of bot micro-buys to inflate the holder count. The creator holds 18.26% (GMGN rat-trader share is also 18.26%). At least 10 other 济公 tokens were launched in the past few hours and all now show roughly zero liquidity. By my later fetch the price had already slipped from $7.4e-5 to $6.4e-5.

authenticity.evidence: Buys and sells in the last 5 minutes are exactly equal (141/141 and 136/136) with about 49 buyers and 49 sellers. There are 1,917 unique buyers against 50 unique sellers, and about 1,300 of those buyers arrived in a single 15-minute window. There are no socials, no website and no DexScreener profile, and GMGN shows only 2 page visits. Web searches for the contract address and the name found nothing.
authenticity.uncertainty: I cannot see X posts or private Chinese Telegram groups, where a real call might exist.

structural_risks: The creator-provided PumpSwap liquidity is 0% locked or burned and can be pulled at any time
Liquidity is about 78% of mcap, so the pool itself is the creator's exit
The pattern of 10+ dead same-name clones points to a serial rug farm
